$comment: Local IPC only. Device-local application names, the hostnames of sites Velvt could not categorize, and salted identifiers; never uploaded, logged, or included in crash diagnostics.
title: UnclassifiedTriage

entries.description: Applications and browser sites together, ranked by seconds_observed, longest first, then applications ahead of sites, then by stable_id. Capped at 8 and floored at 5 minutes observed: a list of thirty one-second curiosities is not a task anyone will do. An empty array is the good state.

items.$comment: stable_id is the only identifier, on purpose. For an application, the bundle identity that lets a saved rule survive a rename is looked up in Rust from the rows it already holds when set_application_category comes back. Protocol 33 replaced app_stable_id with kind and stable_id so one list can hold sites.

kind.description: Which answer this row takes: set_application_category for an application, set_site_category for a site.

stable_id.description: The salted application key or site key, returned verbatim as app_stable_id or site_stable_id.

display_name.description: Display text only. For an application, the device-local name Velvt holds, or null when it holds none; the client shows its own placeholder and never sends one back as a rule name. For a site, its hostname, never null.

window_days.description: The window the entries were computed over, after clamping.
